leaders.notes: Widely described as Point Park's most controversial modern leader; departed after a little over a year amid an admissions scandal and a breakdown of internal communication. Succeeded by Katherine Henderson in 1997.

First woman to serve as president of Point Park; led the institution for nine years before retiring from the role in summer 2006 (Hennigan took over Sept. 1, 2006). Returned to California to direct OLLI at Dominican until retiring in 2021; died in 2022.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President of Finance and Operations
leaders.notes: Rose through Point Park's own administration (VP of finance and operations from 2000), named acting president Jan. 2006 and president Sept. 2006; Point Park's longest-serving modern president (about 15 years). Survived a 2017 faculty no-confidence vote; announced retirement in Oct. 2020, effective 2021.

Started July 2021; resigned abruptly in January 2023 after only about 18 months in office, citing private, personal and family reasons. Previously spent 15 years in leadership roles at Ferris State University before Georgia Highlands.

leaders.priorInstitution: The Hill Group Inc. (national management consulting firm)
leaders.notes: Named interim president in February 2023 after Green's abrupt resignation; the board of trustees unanimously removed 'interim' from his title later in 2023, making him Point Park's ninth president. Longtime Pittsburgh-region business consultant and adjunct professor at Carnegie Mellon's Heinz College; current sitting president.

university: Pontifical Catholic University of Puerto Rico-Arecibo
system: Pontifical Catholic University of Puerto Rico
statusNote: Arecibo is a branch campus of the Pontificia Universidad Catolica de Puerto Rico (PUCPR), headquartered in Ponce. It is led locally by a campus Rector who reports to the university-wide President (see the separate Pontifical Catholic University of Puerto Rico-Ponce record for that office's succession). Public, English-searchable records of the Arecibo campus Rector role are thin; only the two most recent rectors could be confirmed, with approximate/inferred years, and no reliable history reaching back to 1996 was found.

leaders.notes: Confirmed as Rectora of the Arecibo campus in PUCPR's 2019-2020 and 2020-2021 graduation programs. Exact start date and prior/subsequent career not confirmed in available sources; end year of 2021 is inferred from when Edwin Hernandez Vera first appears in the role.

Current Rector of the PUCPR Arecibo campus; confirmed in the role as of 2021 and still serving as of the 2025 graduation ceremonies. Exact appointment date not confirmed in public sources; start year of 2021 is a best-estimate inference.

university: Pontifical Catholic University of Puerto Rico-Ponce
system: Pontifical Catholic University of Puerto Rico
statusNote: Ponce is the main/headquarters campus of the Pontificia Universidad Catolica de Puerto Rico (PUCPR, founded 1948). Unlike the Arecibo and Mayaguez branch campuses, Ponce has no separate campus Rector; it is led directly by the university-wide President, whose succession is recorded here. PUCPR also has a ceremonial 'Grand Chancellor' role held by a Puerto Rico bishop (currently the Bishop of Arecibo); this is a Church-oversight title, not the operating head, so it is not included in the leaders list. Two multi-year gaps in the presidential timeline (circa 1996-1998 and 2002-2006) could not be resolved to a named leader from available public sources.

leaders.priorTitle: Founding priest (Congregation of the Holy Spirit); founder of the Arecibo campus
leaders.priorInstitution: Pontifical Catholic University of Puerto Rico-Arecibo
leaders.notes: Italian-born Holy Ghost Father priest who founded PUCPR's Arecibo campus and later served as university president for about twelve years, presiding when the university received the 'Pontificia' title from the Holy See in 1991. Sources conflict on his exact end date (accounts range from 1996 to as late as 2001); no confirmed named successor is documented until Jose Alberto Morales in 1998.

leaders.priorInstitution: Pontifical Catholic University of Puerto Rico
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: Pontifical Catholic University of Puerto Rico School of Law
leaders.notes: Returned to the PUCPR law faculty after his presidency and taught until retiring in July 2020, after 52 years associated with the university (he called it his intellectual and spiritual home). The gap between Giangiacomo's departure (circa 1996) and his confirmed 1998 start could not be filled with a named leader.

First woman to serve as PUCPR president; led the university's 2005 affiliation with HETS (Hispanic Educational Technology Services) and concluded her term in 2009. The gap between Morales's 2002 departure and her 2006 start could not be filled with a named leader from available sources.

leaders.priorTitle: Rector, University of Puerto Rico at Mayaguez (RUM)
leaders.priorInstitution: University of Puerto Rico at Mayaguez
leaders.notes: Designated president in November 2009 after seven years as rector of UPR-Mayaguez; served roughly 14.5 years across two terms, overseeing a $50 million infrastructure program spanning the Arecibo, Mayaguez and Ponce campuses. Retired in August 2024.

leaders.priorInstitution: Pontifical Catholic University of Puerto Rico
leaders.notes: Took office August 6, 2024, chosen after a selection process involving six candidates and approved by the Vatican's Dicastery for Culture and Education. Previously dean of the PUCPR School of Law and dean of administration at UPR-Mayaguez before becoming VP of Administrative Affairs in Oct. 2018. Current sitting president.

statusNote: Purdue Global was created in 2018 when Purdue University acquired the for-profit Kaplan University and converted it into a public, primarily online institution within the Purdue system; leadership history therefore begins in 2018, not 1996.

leaders.notes: Inaugural chancellor of Purdue University Global at its 2018 launch, having previously led Kaplan University, the for-profit institution Purdue acquired to create Purdue Global. Stepped down effective April 3, 2020, to take a chief content officer role at an ed-tech company.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior Vice Provost for Teaching and Learning
leaders.notes: Had been tasked by then-Purdue President Mitch Daniels with integrating Purdue Global into the Purdue system at its 2018 launch, before becoming chancellor in 2020. Purdue Global saw record retention and 20%+ enrollment growth under his tenure; he stepped down at the end of 2024 to return to the College of Agriculture faculty and take his first career sabbatical.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior Advisor to the Purdue University Provost
leaders.notes: Named interim chancellor effective January 1, 2025. Previously served as Purdue Global provost from August 2020 to January 2024, then as senior advisor to Purdue Provost Patrick Wolfe; has been on the Purdue faculty (Earth, Atmospheric and Planetary Sciences) since 1994 and also held roles as AVP for Research and AVP for Teaching and Learning. Current interim chancellor as Purdue searches for a permanent successor.
